threads.body: This hard cast to `JacksonJsonpGenerator` can throw `ClassCastException` if a `JacksonJsonpMapper` is paired with a non-standard `jsonProvider()` implementation (e.g., subclass overrides provider). In that case, body extraction will fail and return null. Consider guarding with `instanceof JacksonJsonpGenerator` and falling back to the generic `JsonpUtils` serialization path when the provider doesn’t return a Jackson-backed generator.

replies.body:
Addressed in ebfd773aee67f832abc7ccd435d809ea17a3d8da.

Analysis: The mapper type does not guarantee that an overridden provider returns a Jackson-backed generator. The extractor now inspects the generated value and uses `JsonpUtils` for a non-Jackson generator.

Upsides: Custom mapper subclasses keep body capture and sanitization instead of losing the body to a `ClassCastException`.

Downsides: The fallback delegates generated request serialization through `JsonpUtils`, which adds one type check before serialization.

threads.body: Narrowing the catch from `Exception` to `RuntimeException` increases the chance this instrumentation code can propagate unexpected failures (notably `LinkageError`/`NoClassDefFoundError` from optional dependencies or classloader edge cases in a javaagent context). To keep extraction failures from impacting the host app, it’s safer here to catch `Throwable` (or at least `Exception` + `LinkageError`) and return null as before.

replies.body:
Addressed in 17acdad34290d6289f45082b305d14ba11d51d36.

Analysis: Body extraction runs inside javaagent advice and must not affect application requests. Catching `Throwable` at the extraction boundary contains linkage failures as well as serialization exceptions.

Upsides: Optional dependency and classloader failures now disable body capture without breaking the host application.

Downsides: Serious virtual machine errors are also logged and suppressed at this instrumentation boundary.

threads.body: This assertion is brittle across Jackson versions/config because the exact escape casing/formatting (e.g., `\\u00E9` vs `\\u00e9`, spacing, ordering) can change while still honoring `ESCAPE_NON_ASCII`. To make the test more robust while still proving the JsonFactory is used, assert the output does not contain the literal `é` and does contain a Unicode escape sequence, and separately assert the value sanitization (`\"?\"`) is applied.

replies.body:
Addressed in 1ed62df1834a2bacbaaeaacc531bcdce9ec0f78e.

Analysis: The test only needs to prove that non-ASCII escaping comes from the mapper's factory and that sanitization remains active. Exact JSON text also couples it to unrelated formatting choices.

Upsides: The test accepts equivalent Jackson output while still checking both factory reuse and sanitization.

Downsides: The test no longer checks the complete serialized document byte for byte.
